input.quote: 11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years.
input.rationale: Section 11 commits us to a five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals, and the only exit rights are for material breach or insolvency (11.2) plus the acceptance-test and warranty remedies in Sections 3 and 7. There is no Corio right to terminate for convenience during a multi-year term, which is walk-away territory under the rule; the 30-day notice in 11.1 only prevents renewal at the end of a term. Commerce One likewise has no convenience right, so the fix is one-sided in our favour and does not disturb the existing bargain. We inserted a new 11.1A giving Corio convenience termination on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, matching the preferred position, and confirming Commerce One has no reciprocal convenience right.

proposal.summary: Add a Corio right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The five-year term gives us no right to exit without cause, so we have added a convenience termination right on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, consistent with our standard position. If helpful, we can move to sixty (60) days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: 11.1A Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, without penalty, early termination charge or other liability, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio, within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination, any prepaid fees allocable to the period after such effective date. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience.
